title: Localizing a coefficient algebra preserves one Tor vanishing
statement: Let A, B and C be commutative rings, φ : A → B a ring homomorphism, S a multiplicative submonoid of B, and C a localization of B at S, with structure map b : B → C [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For any A-module N and integer j ≥ 0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], if Tor^A_j(B,N) = 0, using φ for the B scalar structure, then Tor^A_j(C,N) = 0, using b ∘ φ for the C scalar structure. No finiteness assumptions are imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, (1) to (2), source-algebra localization; omitted argument expanded by U4; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B67

proof.text: Construct the canonical A-linear coefficient map f : B → C. For each class x in Tor_j(C,N), use the denominator lemma to obtain a unit u and y in Tor_j(B,N) with Tor_j(mul_u,N)(x)=Tor_j(f,N)(y). The assumed IsZero makes y zero, so its image is zero. Multiplication by u on C is an A-linear isomorphism; functoriality of Tor sends it to an isomorphism. Its injectivity gives x=0. Therefore Tor_j(C,N) is a subsingleton module, equivalently IsZero.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B67, localization step, reduced by Q1 to clearing denominators and functoriality on units

theorem isZero_tor_localized_algebra
    (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (φ : A →+* B) [Algebra B C] (S : Submonoid B) [IsLocalization S C]
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} A) (j : ℕ)
    (h : IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
      ((restrictScalars φ).obj (of B B))).obj N)) :
    IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
      ((restrictScalars ((algebraMap B C).comp φ)).obj (of C C))).obj N)
